evidenceClaims.statement: Multiphasic contrast CT can evaluate postoperative collections and associated hepatic vascular injury.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Hepatobiliary-contrast MR cholangiography can localize biliary leakage and assess duct continuity after initial collection assessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline; contrast excretion and peripheral-duct visualization can be limited. This does not require MRCP before every therapeutic ERCP.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Hepatobiliary scintigraphy can detect active leakage but offers less anatomical detail for duct mapping than MR cholangiography.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: CT collection morphology cannot by itself establish the precise ductal source or active state of a bile leak.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A negative retrograde duct injection does not assess an aberrant or disconnected duct that it fails to opacify.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Persistent communicating postoperative bile leakage can be treated with endoscopic transpapillary plastic stenting after collection control.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Complete common hepatic or common bile duct transection is outside the routine transpapillary plastic-stent leak pathway.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Complex duct injuries warrant specialist HPB management when local reconstructive expertise is lacking.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Referral is supported independently of a universal reconstruction date; current repair-timing disagreement is withheld.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Diffuse biliary peritonitis after major duct injury requires urgent abdominal lavage and drainage for source control.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline; resuscitation and antimicrobials are concurrent hospital care, not competing answers.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Late major postcholecystectomy duct injury with a clinically significant stricture may require specialist Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline; not every benign narrowing requires surgery. Proposed surgery follows failure to restore drainage endoscopically.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Benign duct strictures with endoscopically accessible continuity may be treated using temporary multiple plastic stents or a fully covered removable metal stent.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Targeted older society guidance; do not infer all complete occlusions are endoscopically traversable.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: An isolated right hepatic artery interruption may be tolerated when portal perfusion is maintained; its presence does not automatically establish liver necrosis or require immediate arterial reconstruction.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Observational evidence and expert practice; specialist surveillance and individual anatomy govern management.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A fully assessed, completely removed margin-negative gallbladder carcinoma limited to the lamina propria generally does not require completion radical resection.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Gallbladder muscular invasion is outside the lamina-propria-limited T1a postoperative pathway and warrants HPB oncologic reassessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Sources differ on strength of evidence for automatic T1b re-resection; exact additional operation is withheld.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: For a fit patient with localized incidental gallbladder carcinoma extending into perimuscular tissue, completion liver-bed resection and regional portal lymphadenectomy are supported specialist options.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Extrahepatic bile-duct resection during gallbladder cancer completion surgery is reserved for margin clearance or direct involvement rather than added routinely.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One adequate society consensus for the precise duct-margin boundary; 2015 guidance requires current HPB review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A type I bile duct cyst is generally managed by affected extrahepatic duct excision and Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy rather than a cyst-enteric drainage operation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate narrative review; no exact cancer risk or operative deadline is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A symptomatic choledochocele causing biliary obstruction or recurrent pancreatitis can be treated endoscopically by sphincterotomy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate narrative review; does not mandate intervention for an asymptomatic incidental cyst or a solid neoplasm.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Residual biliary tissue can develop late complications or malignancy after cyst excision, so excision does not establish absence of a future surveillance need.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No exact surveillance interval is keyed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: For jaundiced distal extrahepatic strictures without a pancreatic mass, combined EUS-guided and ERCP-based tissue acquisition is supported.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Negative or nondiagnostic biliary brushing does not reliably exclude malignancy in a persistent suspicious stricture.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: For an indeterminate biliary stricture after standard ERCP sampling, cholangioscopy-guided intraductal biopsy is an additional supported diagnostic approach.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Needle sampling of a potentially curable perihilar primary can risk tumor dissemination and should not be substituted automatically for intraductal sampling.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No seeding probability or universal transplant eligibility is asserted; nodal or distant-lesion sampling is a different target.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Perihilar stricture tissue evaluation can combine ERCP brush cytology and fluoroscopy-guided intraductal biopsies.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: When preoperative perihilar drainage is selected, the future liver remnant is the initial drainage target; additional segments depend on response or cholangitis.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate current guideline for exact side selection; no universal ERCP-versus-PTC ranking or remnant-volume cutoff is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: For durable palliation of unresectable distal malignant biliary obstruction, a self-expanding metal stent is favored over repeated plastic stenting.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: After failed ERCP drainage of distal malignant obstruction, expert EUS-guided biliary drainage is favored over percutaneous drainage when appropriate local expertise exists.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate current guideline; percutaneous drainage remains a supported alternative when EUS drainage is unavailable or unsuitable.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Older WSES and newer SAGES-AHPBA recommendations use different repair-time categories and allow context-dependent exceptions; a universal repair-date key is not supported by this packet.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Withheld scoring. No averaging of intervals; clinician must adjudicate the exact proposed scenario.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Type I bile duct cysts involve the extrahepatic bile duct.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single specialist review; no inherited ethnicity variable is used.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Type IVA bile duct cysts include intrahepatic and extrahepatic cystic disease.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single specialist review; no inherited ethnicity variable is used.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A choledochocele is cystic expansion of the intraduodenal distal bile duct.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single specialist review; no inherited ethnicity variable is used.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A localized postoperative bile collection can require percutaneous drainage when it is not adequately drained.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline; source control depends on localization and clinical condition.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: Bile duct cystic disease confined to a defined intrahepatic segment can be considered for segment-directed liver resection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single specialist narrative review; no blanket resection or transplant eligibility rule is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A benign duct stricture is treated with temporary removable stent strategies rather than routine permanent uncovered metal stenting.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Targeted society-guideline verification; device selection is individualized, and plastic versus removable covered metal superiority is not taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A localized postoperative biloma may be managed by percutaneous catheter drainage when its anatomy permits access.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Operative source control remains appropriate for diffuse contamination or when percutaneous control is not feasible; no universal access-method superiority is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the exact postoperative or perihilar anatomy described in the revised clinic-chart-review candidate.

evidenceClaims.statement: ESGE 2018 does not recommend a primary endoscopic approach for draining bilomas.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Strong recommendation based on low-quality evidence; selected expert EUS drainage exists, so the item asks for the initial preferred approach rather than an impossible alternative.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the exact postoperative or perihilar anatomy described in the revised clinic-chart-review candidate.

evidenceClaims.statement: Transhepatic biliary drainage can provide decompression in septic patients with complete main-duct obstruction when ERCP cannot restore drainage.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline, weak/low-quality management evidence; not a universal timing or definitive-repair rule.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the exact postoperative or perihilar anatomy described in the revised clinic-chart-review candidate.

evidenceClaims.statement: Cholangitis in a residual obstructed biliary territory can require additional drainage despite drainage of the planned future liver remnant.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate current guideline, recommendation 23; the exact territory requires current anatomical and infection findings.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the exact postoperative or perihilar anatomy described in the revised clinic-chart-review candidate.

evidenceClaims.statement: ESGE 2026 suggests temporary multiple plastic stents for postcholecystectomy benign biliary strictures.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Weak recommendation. This does not establish superiority over every expert covered-metal strategy in every patient.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the exact postoperative or perihilar anatomy described in the revised clinic-chart-review candidate.

evidenceClaims.statement: ESGE 2026 describes covered metal stenting as an option for postcholecystectomy strictures more than 2 cm below the hepatic confluence or when adherence to repeated ERCP is problematic.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The exact 2-cm boundary is directly stated in recommendation 1. No universal contraindication or fixed exchange interval is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the exact postoperative or perihilar anatomy described in the revised clinic-chart-review candidate.

evidenceClaims.statement: A cyst-enteric drainage operation leaves abnormal bile-duct cyst epithelium in place.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate specialist review; postoperative symptom relief does not establish complete cyst removal.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the exact postoperative or perihilar anatomy described in the revised clinic-chart-review candidate.

evidenceClaims.statement: Bile-duct cyst drainage procedures retain a greater metachronous cancer concern than excision and are not the recommended definitive type I treatment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single specialist review; no exact malignancy probability, operative deadline or universal intrapancreatic resection extent is keyed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the exact postoperative or perihilar anatomy described in the revised clinic-chart-review candidate.

evidenceClaims.statement: An isolated right hepatic artery interruption may be tolerated when portal perfusion is maintained; its presence does not automatically establish liver necrosis or require immediate arterial reconstruction.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Observational evidence and expert practice; specialist surveillance and individual anatomy govern management.

evidenceClaims.statement: A fully assessed, completely removed margin-negative gallbladder carcinoma limited to the lamina propria generally does not require completion radical resection.

evidenceClaims.statement: Gallbladder muscular invasion is outside the lamina-propria-limited T1a postoperative pathway and warrants HPB oncologic reassessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Sources differ on strength of evidence for automatic T1b re-resection; exact additional operation is withheld.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: For a fit patient with localized incidental gallbladder carcinoma extending into perimuscular tissue, completion liver-bed resection and regional portal lymphadenectomy are supported specialist options.

evidenceClaims.statement: Extrahepatic bile-duct resection during gallbladder cancer completion surgery is reserved for margin clearance or direct involvement rather than added routinely.

evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A type I bile duct cyst is generally managed by affected extrahepatic duct excision and Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy rather than a cyst-enteric drainage operation.

evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specifically described biliary anatomy and care phase

evidenceClaims.statement: A symptomatic choledochocele causing biliary obstruction or recurrent pancreatitis can be treated endoscopically by sphincterotomy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate narrative review; does not mandate intervention for an asymptomatic incidental cyst or a solid neoplasm.

evidenceClaims.statement: Residual biliary tissue can develop late complications or malignancy after cyst excision, so excision does not establish absence of a future surveillance need.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No exact surveillance interval is keyed.

evidenceClaims.statement: For jaundiced distal extrahepatic strictures without a pancreatic mass, combined EUS-guided and ERCP-based tissue acquisition is supported.

evidenceClaims.statement: Negative or nondiagnostic biliary brushing does not reliably exclude malignancy in a persistent suspicious stricture.

evidenceClaims.statement: Needle sampling of a potentially curable perihilar primary can risk tumor dissemination and should not be substituted automatically for intraductal sampling.

evidenceClaims.statement: When preoperative perihilar drainage is selected, the future liver remnant is the initial drainage target; additional segments depend on response or cholangitis.

evidenceClaims.statement: Older WSES and newer SAGES-AHPBA recommendations use different repair-time categories and allow context-dependent exceptions; a universal repair-date key is not supported by this packet.
